card.name: "Or" after disease progression in dosing
card.fires_on: The word "or" right after "until disease progression" in oncology dosing instructions, just before "unacceptable toxicity". Also fires on a verb like "provide" in a similar spot, after "appears to".

modes.label: Or before unacceptable toxicity
modes.description: The word "or" linking disease progression to unacceptable toxicity in treatment-duration sentences.
modes.example: Continue CYRAMZA until disease progression<< or>> unacceptable toxicity.

modes.label: Provide after appears to
modes.description: The verb "provide" in a sentence about a target AUC giving an appropriate dose range.
modes.example: using single-agent carboplatin appears to<< provide>> the most appropriate dose range in previously treated

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about handling or tackling something and away from words about effectiveness or efficacy.
card.plain: It marks the spot in cancer dosing text where treatment continues until the disease progresses or side effects become unacceptable.
